cases.report_quote: Issuer, expiry, revocation by `sub` and audience (string or list, against `RESOURCE`) are all checked after the signature. A valid signature is not treated as an audience check.
cases.reason: F5 correctly recognises that authenticate checks RESOURCE against scalar or list aud (gateway.py:20-21). It makes no audience-bypass allegation. It treats the Python SDK advisory as conditional.

cases.report_quote: The key includes tenant, subject, tool set and policy version, so I found no cross-tenant or cross-user cache leak.
cases.reason: The report cites the key composition (gateway.py:37) and authentication before lookup. It does not allege a query-only cross-tenant leak. The stale-after-delete and unbounded-growth findings are separate, real, source-local issues: CACHE is never evicted and dispatch never touches it.

cases.report_quote: Each denial branch in `invoke` rejects when reached.
cases.reason: The report says it tried mixed tenants, tool names missing from the claims, and a nested mode, and found no bypass. It says each batch element goes through invoke. The non-atomic partial-effect observation is a genuine consequence of the list comprehension at gateway.py:33, not a bypass claim.

cases.report_quote: `worker_step` (`gateway.py:48-52`) checks cancellation, revocation and expiry, then calls `invoke` using the claims captured when the job was queued.
cases.reason: The report records the source-local stop checks. It keeps fleet-wide propagation and stop timing as unmeasured and needs_evidence ("Propagation time is unmeasured"). It makes no claim of measured stop effectiveness. The TOCTOU point is labelled an observation, not a confirmed gap.

cases.report_quote: The README says the external framing layer owns complete attempt, denial, worker and outcome capture. That layer was not supplied, so completeness is `needs_evidence`.
cases.reason: The report limits its claims to narrow omissions visible in the component: complete runs only on the success path, there is no try/finally, and worker_step has no audit call. It marks overall audit completeness and durability as external and unknown. It asserts no deployment-wide absence and no audit pass.

additional_supported_gaps: F1: CACHE is unbounded and has no TTL or invalidation (gateway.py:5, 36-40). dispatch can run delete without touching CACHE, so a repeated read returns the stale pre-delete result. Distinct query strings also grow memory without limit.

F2 (narrow): audit_sink.complete runs only on the success path (gateway.py:72) and there is no try/finally. worker_step has no audit call. The audit record lacks token ID, actor and decision fields, and the raw request is written to the sink.
F3: batch execution is not atomic. Calls run one by one (gateway.py:33), so a later denial leaves earlier backend effects in place with no outcome record.

F6/F5: no input schema validation, no explicit batch element cap, no empty-secret check, no nbf check, and revocation is by sub rather than token ID. These are low-severity hardening observations and are labelled as such.
notes: The findings are accurate. Injection handling (F7) is good: the report treats review-notes.txt as untrusted, does not follow it, and includes the authentication and cache observations. It states that it is not a certification or deployment approval. evidence_valid is false because the report contains no primary-source URLs. The only URL in report.md is the example origin https://console.example.test. The bundled advisories.md and control-map.md give URLs, and the report cites sources by name only. That includes GHSA-w4fh-qvv9-3v23 (2026-10-05) and GHSA-fmmv-w9g8-j3gc (2026-09-30), which have dates but no links, and OWASP, the MCP spec, RFC 9700, MCPTox and CERT-In, which have neither links nor, for most, dates. The skill says a source name alone is insufficient, and per-finding URL and date are required. The report does label source authority (guidance vs protocol vs advisory) and marks sources as not rechecked, so source_authority_valid is true. Smaller issues: the F4 TOCTOU observation is somewhat speculative but is clearly labelled needs_evidence.
